content_preview.title: GitSpawn Flaws Let Malicious .git Configs Run Attacker Code in Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and Other AI Coding Agents
content_preview.summary: Manifold Security found eight flaws across seven AI coding agents that let a repository's git config silently execute code the moment it is opened.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Manifold Security has disclosed eight security flaws, collectively named "GitSpawn," across seven command-line AI coding agents, according to [The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/09/malicious-git-configs-can-make-claude.html). The flaws let a repository's own git configuration specify a command that runs on a developer's machine the moment an AI coding agent opens the project, according to [Cyber Security News](https://cybersecuritynews.com/gitspawn-flaws-execute-code/)....

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece at 606 words, within the 400-1200 word range for the category. Clear section hierarchy (Overview, What We Know, Mitigation, What We Don't Know). Attributions ('according to...') are attached to nearly every factual sentence, which is appropriate for a multi-source security disclosure story. The 'What We Don't Know' closer is a good editorial practice that honestly scopes the story's limits.
editor_notes.source_verification: 3 sources cited; 2 of 3 verified via committed gzipped snapshot, 1 verified via live WebFetch fallback because the snapshot fetch failed. (1) source-0.html.gz (thehackernews.com, HTTP 200): confirmed the eight-flaws/seven-agents count, the 'GitSpawn' name, the core.fsmonitor mechanism description, the .git-directory-intact precondition, the patched/unpatched agent list (goose, Claude Code, Cursor patched; Hermes Agent, Qwen Code, Grok Build, and a second Claude Code path unpatched as of Sept 1), the per-agent execution-timing sentence (workspace-trust prompt / authentication / first keystroke), and the Manifold quote 'The vulnerability is not in the model, or in anything new...' — this quote is VERBATIM in the snapshot, confirmed exact match. (2) source-2.html.gz (github.com goose security advisory GHSA-r5pp-p5r8-466r, HTTP 200): confirmed CVE-2026-72718, CVSS 4.0 base score 7.0 (High), credit to Francisco Rosales of Manifold Security, and 'all versions before 1.44.0 affected, patched in 1.44.0.' However, the article presents a 'direct quote' from this advisory that is NOT verbatim — see Concerns. (3) cybersecuritynews.com/gitspawn-flaws-execute-code/ — snapshot fetch failed with HTTP 403 (bot-blocked, manifest 'file': null, no archive_fallback available). Per review policy, used a live WebFetch as a last-resort fallback (not the committed snapshot) to attempt verification: the fallback fetch corroborated the article's quoted sentence about repository delivery ('through a zipped folder, a shared drive, a synced directory, or a USB stick, exactly the way colleagues and consultants routinely hand off projects' — reproduced verbatim across two independent fetches of the live page) and broadly corroborated the patched/vulnerable agent lists attributed to this outlet. This verification is NOT based on the provenance-committed snapshot and is inherently weaker; flagged as a clarification below.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: The technical mechanism (core.fsmonitor executed during git status/diff index refresh), the CVE/CVSS details for goose, the agent-by-agent patch status, and the per-agent execution-timing claims all check out against the two readable snapshots. One issue found: the block quoted from the GitHub security advisory and attributed to it ('The goose review command executes system git without sanitizing user-controlled configurations. A malicious repository containing a [core] fsmonitor setting in .git/config triggers arbitrary command execution when git refreshes its index during diff operations—before any model interaction or approval occurs.') is a paraphrase/compression of the advisory's actual text, not a verbatim quote. The advisory actually reads: 'goose review command runs the system git to gather the diff it reviews, without stripping attacker-controlled git config. A malicious repository whose .git/config sets [core] fsmonitor = <command> causes git to execute that command on the host during its index refresh (git diff HEAD). So running goose review inside a malicious repo runs attacker code - no submitted prompt, no model call, no tool approval, no trust prompt. The command executes before goose ever contacts the model.' The substance is accurate but the wording inside the quote marks does not match the source. This is a body-level detail (not headline/summary/lead) and is recoverable with a single corrections note.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout. No sensationalism, no editorializing, no AI self-reference. Appropriately hedges claims that are outlet-specific ('according to The Hacker News' vs 'according to Cyber Security News') rather than presenting contested details as settled fact.
editor_notes.originality: Searched src/content/articles/ for 'gitspawn', 'fsmonitor', 'core.fsmonitor'. Found one unrelated hit: 2026-06/30-git-255-adds-a-git-history-fixup-command-brings-the-fsmonitor-daemon-to-linux-and-lets-git-push-target-remote-groups.md, which covers a Git 2.55 feature release, not this vulnerability disclosure. Also reviewed recent article titles from the last week, including an unrelated AI-coding-agent security story ('Tenet Security's GhostJacking Attack Tricked Claude Code Into Rewriting Cloudflare DNS Records') — a different vulnerability class (prompt-injection-driven DNS rewriting, not git-config-triggered RCE at session startup). No duplicate or substantially overlapping coverage found; this is a genuinely new topic.
concerns: The block quote attributed to the goose GitHub security advisory (CVE-2026-72718) is a paraphrase of the advisory's actual language, not a verbatim reproduction, despite being presented inside quotation marks as a direct quote.

One of three sources (cybersecuritynews.com) could not be captured as a committed snapshot (HTTP 403, bot-blocked); verification of claims attributed to it relies on a live WebFetch fallback rather than the provenance-committed archive.

The article's sentence attributing a patched/vulnerable agent breakdown to Cyber Security News omits that outlet's stated position on Claude Code (per the WebFetch fallback, Cyber Security News lists Claude Code as still vulnerable due to the ultrareview path) — a completeness gap rather than a factual error, since the article does not claim CSN considers Claude Code patched either.
recommendations: File a corrections record for the misquoted goose advisory text (severity: correction).

File a corrections record noting the cybersecuritynews.com source could not be archived and was verified via live fetch rather than snapshot (severity: clarification), consistent with prior precedent (see src/content/corrections/2026-05/20-sony-xperia-1-viii-*.json for the same pattern).
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Substantively solid, well-sourced security disclosure article with accurate technical detail and appropriate multi-outlet attribution. Two recoverable issues — a paraphrased quote presented as verbatim, and one source that could only be verified via a live-fetch fallback rather than a committed snapshot — are each honestly coverable in a corrections note and do not affect the headline, summary, or lead. Recommend APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS.
